data.hook: With their season opener looming, the Saints placed young running back Audric Estime on injured reserve due to a thigh injury, opening doors for practice squad talents to step up.
data.name: Saints Shuffle Roster with Estime on IR Before Lions Opener
data.summary: New Orleans placed 23-year-old Audric Estime on injured reserve, sidelining him for at least four games, while signing tight end Treyton Welch to the active roster and elevating wide receiver Kevin Austin Jr. and undrafted rookie running back CJ Donaldson. These moves add depth amid Alvin Kamara's questionable knee status for Sunday's game at Detroit. The Lions countered by re-signing defensive end Levi Onwuzurike to their practice squad and elevating defensive lineman Ben Stille, typical Week 1 tweaks to handle injuries and salary needs.

data.name: Lions Nearly Full Strength as Saints Face Key Absences in Season Opener
data.summary: The Saints and Lions kick off the 2026 NFL season Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at Ford Field in Detroit, with the Lions boasting a nearly full roster—only DB Christian Izien listed as questionable with a groin injury. New Orleans will miss RB Audric Estime, TE Oscar Delp, and edge rusher Cameron Jordan, while star RB Alvin Kamara remains questionable despite full practice Friday; reports suggest he may still play. If sidelined, the Saints turn to Travis Etienne Jr. and Kendre Miller in the backfield for this physical matchup.

data.hook: Levi Onwuzurike's sudden release from the Lions' active roster caught everyone off guard, just days before their season kickoff against the Saints.
data.name: Lions Release Onwuzurike Before Opener, Re-Sign to Practice Squad
data.summary: The Detroit Lions cut defensive end Levi Onwuzurike, a former second-round pick, and waived rookie Tyre West to avoid guaranteeing Onwuzurike's $1.2 million salary under NFL rules. The team quickly re-signed Onwuzurike to the practice squad and elevated Ben Stille for the game, a standard move to maintain depth without upfront pay commitments. Despite injuries like a torn ACL in 2025, Onwuzurike showed promise in 2024 with 28 tackles and 1.5 sacks, and he could return to the active roster soon if needed on the strong Lions defensive line.

data.hook: The Vikings head into their heated rivalry game with every player ready to go, while the Packers nurse key injury doubts just hours from kickoff.
data.name: Healthy Vikings Face Injured Packers in NFC North Opener
data.summary: Minnesota enters Sunday's season opener at U.S. Bank Stadium with no injury designations, confirming left tackle Christian Darrisaw and safety Harrison Smith are good after rest days. The Vikings elevated outside linebacker Kyle Van Noy and running back DeeJay Dallas from the practice squad for expected playing time. Green Bay lists guard Aaron Banks, tackle Zach Bako-Bewele, and linebacker Ty’Ron Hopper as questionable, with defensive tackle Warren Brinson out due to a calf injury; they elevated wide receiver Bo Melton and linebacker Kristian Welch. Fans on both sides buzz with optimism ahead of the 132nd meeting at 3:25 p.m. CT on CBS.

data.name: Cowboys Face Giants in 2026 NFL Season Opener at MetLife
data.summary: The Dallas Cowboys visit the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on Sunday at 7 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock, kicking off the 2026 NFL season with new Giants head coach John Harbaugh's debut. Giants edge rusher Brian Burns highlighted uncertainty at Dallas' right tackle between Terence Steele and Broderick Jones as an exploit opportunity, while Cowboys fans predict a blowout after last year's 7-9-1 finish. Analysts see Dallas as favorites, but the Giants' pass rush and road atmosphere promise a gritty trench battle in primetime.
